title: Teachers' menu offers seven links that end in "Access denied"
steps: Sign in as a teacher (chinedu.okeke). Click Academics → Sessions, Terms, Classes, Subjects, Periods, or Results & Reports → Subject results, Report cards.
expected: The menu only shows pages a teacher may open (Timetable, attendance, Assessments).
actual: All seven links are shown and each lands on "Access denied".
cause: NavMenu showed the whole Academics and Results sections to the Teacher role, but those pages authorise SuperAdmin and HeadTeacher only.
fix: NavMenu.razor: the admin-only links inside Academics and Results & Reports are rendered only for SuperAdmin / HeadTeacher; teachers keep Timetable and Assessments.

title: Dashboard shows school-wide account statistics to every role and greets people by username
steps: Sign in as a parent (ngozi.okafor) and look at the Dashboard.
expected: A personal welcome by name and content relevant to the role; account statistics only for the administrator.
actual: "Welcome, ngozi.okafor!" and the cards Staff & students 58 / Roles configured 7 / Active users 58 / Deactivated 0 — for parents, pupils and all staff.
cause: Home.razor (Sprint 1) was written for the SuperAdmin and never scoped when other roles were added; the greeting used the login name.
fix: Home.razor: greets by first name; the account statistics show only for SuperAdmin; every other role sees shortcut cards to its own pages.

title: Dashboard and header icons render as empty boxes
steps: Sign in as superadmin and look at the dashboard statistic cards and the header (user chip, Sign out).
expected: Each card and header button shows its icon.
actual: Six blank icon placeholders (dashboard cards, header user chip, Sign out); the same markup on the sign-in, sign-out and access-denied pages.
cause: Icons were written as ; Radzen's icon font draws the glyph from the icon name as text, so an empty span shows nothing.
fix: Home.razor uses ; MainLayout and the Account pages write the icon name inside the span (logout).

title: Users, Students and Parents lists are empty until a filter is used
steps: Open User Management → All Users (or Family → Students / Parents) without touching the filters.
expected: The first page of records is listed immediately.
actual: "No users match your filters." (and the same for students and parents) until a search or filter is changed.
cause: The grids load pages on the server (Radzen LoadData) but their data field started as an empty list; Radzen only requests the first page when Data is null. (Same issue fixed on the Audit log page in Sprint 16.)
fix: Users.razor, Students.razor, Parents.razor: the grid data starts as null.

title: A teacher can be timetabled in two classes in the same period
steps: Timetable → First Term, Primary 4A → Monday / Period 2 → Mathematics, teacher Chinedu Okeke (who teaches Primary 5A then) → Save.
expected: Refused: the teacher is already teaching Primary 5A at that time.
cause: TimetableService.UpsertEntryAsync only enforced one lesson per class per slot; it never checked the teacher's other classes.
fix: TimetableService.UpsertEntryAsync refuses a teacher who already has a lesson in another class in the same term, day and period, naming the clash.

title: Deactivating a parent or pupil does not stop their portal login
steps: Open a parent (or pupil) record and press Deactivate. Sign in with that family member's portal username and password.
expected: Sign-in is refused while the record is inactive (as it is for deactivated staff), and works again after Activate.
actual: The deactivated parent signs straight in to the portal.
cause: ParentService / StudentService.SetActiveAsync only flipped the family record's IsActive flag; the Sprint 9 portal account (ApplicationUser) stayed active.
fix: New PortalAccounts helper: deactivating/activating a parent or pupil record now deactivates/reactivates the linked login the same way User Management does (IsActive, lockout, new security stamp to end open sessions).

title: Attendance registers can be opened for future dates
steps: Daily attendance → Primary 5A → a date one week ahead → Open register.
expected: Refused — attendance records what happened, so it can't be taken in advance.
actual: "Register opened." with every pupil marked Present for next week.
cause: DailyAttendanceService.OpenAsync (and SubjectAttendanceService.OpenAsync) validated the term and weekday but not that the date had arrived.
fix: Both services refuse a date after today in the school's time zone (Notifications:TimeZone, Africa/Lagos).

title: A discount can push a paid invoice into a negative balance
steps: Open a fully paid invoice (Chiamaka Okafor) and enter a ₦10,000 discount on the Tuition line.
expected: Refused — the invoice is settled; money already received must be refunded instead.
actual: "Discount applied."; the invoice shows Balance −₦10,000.00 and stays Paid.
cause: InvoiceService.SetLineDiscountAsync only checked the discount against the line amount, not against what had already been paid.
fix: SetLineDiscountAsync refuses a discount that would bring the amount due below the amount paid, and says how much discount is still possible.

title: Refunding a payment does not restore the invoice balance
steps: Record a ₦100,000 payment on an invoice, open the receipt and press Refund, then open the invoice.
expected: The receipt shows Refunded and the invoice balance goes back up by ₦100,000.
actual: "Payment refunded." but the invoice still counts the ₦100,000 as paid (balance ₦112,000 instead of ₦212,000; status Partially Paid).
cause: The refund soft-deletes the payment's allocations, then InvoiceService.RecomputeInvoiceTotalsAsync sums invoice.Allocations. EF Core's relationship fix-up keeps the soft-deleted rows (still tracked) in that collection, so the refunded money still counted. Same root cause as the Sprint 10 parent-deletion hotfix.
fix: Invoice totals and the cancel/delete guards ignore soft-deleted or removed allocations (InvoiceService.LiveAllocations); PaymentService's delete guard does the same.

title: Parents and pupils cannot open a published report card
steps: As a parent: My wards → Chiamaka → Report cards → view (eye) button. As a pupil: My results → view button.
expected: The published report card opens, read-only.
actual: "Access denied" — the buttons link to the staff report-card page (/reports/{id}), which only SuperAdmin and HeadTeacher may open.
cause: Sprint 8 reused the staff editing page for the portal links instead of giving families a view of their own.
fix: New read-only page /portal/report-cards/{id} (PortalReportCard.razor): a pupil sees only their own published cards, a parent only their linked wards' published cards, with a Print button. The portal links now point there; the staff page stays staff-only.

title: Over-issue message is garbled
steps: Record movement → Whiteboard markers (4 on hand) → Issue 50 → Save.
expected: A clear refusal, e.g. "Cannot remove 50 of 'Whiteboard markers': only 4 on hand."
cause: A word was missing from the message template in StockMovementService, and quantities were printed with three decimals.
fix: Message reworded; quantities print without trailing zeros.

title: Invoice page's Discount card shows the word "DISCOUNT" over the amount
expected: The Discount card shows an icon like the other three cards.
actual: The icon renders as the text "DISCOUNT" in large letters across the discount amount. Found by reviewing the FIN-06 screenshot (the case's scripted checks passed).
cause: InvoiceDetail.razor used the icon name "discount", which is not in the icon font bundled with Radzen, so the browser shows the name as text.
fix: Uses the "local_offer" (price tag) icon instead. The UAT runner now flags any icon drawn as text on every page it visits.
